# Known scanner findings in N|Solid for Node.js 22

<!-- Generated by tools/vex/generate.py from exceptions.json. Edit that file, then run generate.py. -->

Scanners that match package versions report these CVEs in packages that N|Solid installs. Each one is fixed in N|Solid's copy or doesn't affect N|Solid. [nsolid.openvex.json](nsolid.openvex.json) records the same statuses as an OpenVEX document, for scanners that can import one.

Paths are relative to the N|Solid installation directory: `/usr/local` in NodeSource's container images, or the directory a release tarball was extracted to.

| Package | CVE | Status | Path |

## CVE-2026-9496

**pacote 19.0.2: fixed in place.** Upstream fix backported; vulnerable regex replaced with linear indexOf()/slice() logic. Upstream fix: https://github.com/npm/pacote/commit/627a7dc1a214d857472a13b48e42559c75288c9e

To check for the fix, run this in the installation directory:

```sh
grep -q hashIndex lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/pacote/lib/util/add-git-sha.js && echo fixed || echo "not fixed"
```

**pacote 20.0.1: not affected** (vulnerable code not in execute path). npm also carries pacote 20.0.1, which only @npmcli/metavuln-calculator uses: for npm audit, it calls pacote.packument() with the registry names of packages that have advisories. The vulnerable regex is in addGitSha(), which runs only when resolving git dependencies, so it never runs in this copy.

## CVE-2026-48758

**@sigstore/core 2.0.0: not affected** (inline mitigations already exist). Not exploitable through supported npm CLI workflows. The affected DSSE encoding path is exercised, but npm never uses payloadType to select a parser, policy, or authorization decision. It parses the signed JSON payload and independently validates the package subject/name and SHA-512 digest.

## CVE-2026-48815

**sigstore 3.1.0: not affected** (vulnerable code not in execute path). Not exploitable through supported npm CLI workflows. The vulnerability only matters when a caller relies on the certificateOIDs verification option. Pacote passes only TUF cache configuration and an optional key selector, while libnpmpublish calls sigstore.verify(provenanceBundle) without options. npm therefore never requests the constraint that affected Sigstore versions silently discard.

## CVE-2026-93687

**braces 3.0.3, fast-glob 3.3.3, micromatch 4.0.8: not affected** (vulnerable code cannot be controlled by adversary). The stack-exhaustion denial of service (CVE-2026-93687, GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) requires evaluating deeply nested, attacker-controlled brace-expansion patterns. The braces maintainer considers the advisory only exploitable when an application passes user-supplied patterns to braces: hitting a nesting depth of 5,000 already requires more than 10,000 characters of input, and input-length limits (maxLength) are a sufficient, already-supported mitigation (https://github.com/micromatch/braces/issues/70). In N|Solid, braces reaches the runtime only inside the ncm-ng agent through fast-glob -> micromatch -> braces, and every glob pattern ncm-ng evaluates is hardcoded (workers/certifyNG/install-scripts.js and workers/general/getLocalModuleFilePaths.js match fixed patterns such as '\*\*/\*.js' under the user's own working directory), so adversarial brace patterns cannot reach braces through N|Solid. braces has no patched release (every version <= 3.0.3 is affected), so an exemption is the only available remediation. npm audit surfaces this single advisory in deps/ncm-ng as three findings (braces directly, plus the micromatch and fast-glob chain findings), tracked in https://github.com/nodesource/nsolid-dependency-vuln-assessments/issues/2934, https://github.com/nodesource/nsolid-dependency-vuln-assessments/issues/2935 and https://github.com/nodesource/nsolid-dependency-vuln-assessments/issues/2936.

## CVE-2026-118764

**minimatch 9.0.9: fixed in place.** Upstream fixes backported to the minimatch copies bundled with npm and with Node.js: at optimizationLevel 2, the \*\*/.. split pass throws a RangeError rather than make more than braceExpandMax patterns or add more than 1,000,000 path portions, and sets of more than 1000 patterns are not deduplicated. Upstream fixes: https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/commit/77a0f5c4b80bdc641c3c930a1d9edf5ad2db57f8 and https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/pull/336

To check for the fix, run this in the installation directory:

```sh
grep -q 'too many patterns' lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/minimatch/dist/commonjs/index.js && echo fixed || echo "not fixed"
grep -q 'too many patterns' lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/minimatch/dist/esm/index.js && echo fixed || echo "not fixed"
```

## CVE-2026-118772

**joi: not affected** (vulnerable code not in execute path). The quadratic split is in joi's string().email() with the multiple option. joi reaches N|Solid only as a dependency of the ncm-ng agent, which fetches it from the npm registry when the package is built, so its version depends on the build date: builds made since 28 October 2026 get 17.13.9, which has the fix. ncm-ng never calls string().email(), so the affected code never runs in any build.

## CVE-2026-118773

**glob 10.5.0: not affected** (vulnerable code not in execute path). The flaw is in how glob handles an AbortSignal: after an aborted walk rejects, glob keeps reading directories. npm never passes a signal to glob (its callers are the help and help-search commands, @npmcli/map-workspaces, @npmcli/package-json and cacache), so the affected abort branches never run.
